userStories.title: S2 — one clean alembic head; fresh clones boot; stamped databases keep upgrading
userStories.description: THE WAVE'S ONLY M STORY — read PRD-209 S2 + Q1 first. Today: ~168 files under orchestrator/alembic/versions/ with 12 leaf heads; init_complete_schema.sql seeds compose Postgres with NO alembic_version stamp, so a fresh volume replays the whole forest and crashes (relation marketplace_installs does not exist). Deliver ALL FOUR, mechanism your choice: (1) `alembic heads` == exactly 1; (2) a FRESH EMPTY database reaches the head via the supported path (initdb + stamp + upgrade, or a clean baseline replay — whichever you build, the alembic-from-zero lane in test.yml must exercise exactly that supported path and pass); (3) a database stamped at the CURRENT 12-head frontier (= Railway prod) upgrades to the new head with plain `alembic upgrade heads`, NO manual stamp/step — prove with a lineage test that walks down_revision links from the new head and asserts every current frontier revision id is an ancestor; (4) init_complete_schema.sql gains the alembic_version stamp matching the new head id. A pure AST guard asserts len(heads)==1 over the versions dir. If you delete revision files, constraint (3) fails — so DON'T; the approved shape is a merge revision collapsing the 12 heads + the stamp (record in the commit body which variant you built and why it satisfies all four).
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — alembic heads == 1: the 12-head forest was already collapsed by prior merge revisions (PRD-176/203/204/230); `alembic heads` and the AST guard test_prd209_exactly_one_head both return exactly prd_workspace_models_backfill. No new merge revision needed (adding one to a single head is a no-op) — approved merge+stamp shape, NOT a forest squash (would strand prod).

userStories.title: S4 — schema-drift CI lane (the net for four writers of schema truth)
userStories.description: No lane catches models ↔ migration-head divergence (July's 'ALTER-ed-but-never-CREATE-d table' shipped undetected). Build scripts/ci/schema_drift_check.py + a non-required workflow job: construct the schema two ways (applied-migrations shadow vs declared init_complete_schema.sql, or a fresh Base.metadata.create_all dump — pick the pair that catches the known failure class) and diff; exit non-zero on drift. Pure-testable core: test_schema_drift_detects_divergent_column feeds fixture DDL where a model column is absent from the migration head and asserts drift is reported. Wire the job into CI as its own lane (non-required for now — flipping required is the owner's Q2 action).
acceptanceCriteria: DONE — scripts/ci/schema_drift_check.py exists: PURE static parse (no DB, no Base.metadata import — incomplete without ML deps, no live Alembic — the forest doesn't replay from base). diff_schemas() is the table+column diff CORE; the wired check asserts every table a migration ALTERs/add_columns/indexes/FKs is also CREATE-d by a migration or init_complete_schema.sql. test_prd209_schema_drift.py: 12 guards green (local py3.10). Pair chosen = migration-forest ALTERs vs (migration+init) CREATEs — the ONLY pair that catches the KNOWN class: the three cross-writer table diffs (init↔models 63+72, init↔forest 80) are massively divergent by design (create_all fills the gap), so only the intra-writer 'ALTER-ed-but-never-CREATE-d' invariant is both green-able and the real July crash cause (test.yml:410 'crashes on tables that are ALTER-ed but never CREATE-d in the historical forest').
